{{Short description|Large countable ordinal}}
In the mathematical fields of [[set theory]] and [[proof theory]], the '''Takeuti–Feferman–Buchholz ordinal (TFBO)''' is a [[large countable ordinal]], which acts as the limit of the range of [[Buchholz psi functions|Buchholz's psi function]] and Feferman's theta function.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Buchholz's ψ functions|url=https://neugierde.github.io/cantors-attic/Buchholz%27s_%CF%88_functions#takeuti-feferman-buchholz-ordinal|access-date=2021-08-10|website=cantors-attic|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Buchholz's ψ functions|url=https://neugierde.github.io/cantors-attic/Buchholz%27s_%CF%88_functions#takeuti-feferman-buchholz-ordinal|access-date=2021-08-17|website=cantors-attic|language=en-US}}</ref> It was named by David Madore,<ref name=":0" /> after [[Gaisi Takeuti]], [[Solomon Feferman]] and Wilfried Buchholz. It is written as <math>\psi_0(\varepsilon_{\Omega_\omega + 1})</math> using Buchholz's psi function,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2017-07-29|title=A Zoo of Ordinals|url=http://www.madore.org/~david/math/ordinal-zoo.pdf|access-date=2021-08-10|website=Madore}}</ref> an [[ordinal collapsing function]] invented by Wilfried Buchholz,<ref>{{Cite web|date=1981|title=Collapsingfunktionen|url=https://www.mathematik.uni-muenchen.de/~buchholz/articles/Collapsing.pdf|access-date=2021-08-10|website=[[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1986-01-01|title=A new system of proof-theoretic ordinal functions|url=|journal=[[Annals of Pure and Applied Logic]]|language=en|volume=32|pages=195–207|doi=10.1016/0168-0072(86)90052-7|issn=0168-0072|last1=Buchholz|first1=W.|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Buchholz | first1 = Wilfried
 | last2 = Schütte | first2 = Kurt|author2link = Kurt Schütte
 | isbn = 88-7088-166-0
 | location = Naples, Italy
 | publisher = Bibliopolis
 | series = Studies in Proof Theory, Monographs
 | title = Proof Theory of Impredicative Subsystems of Analysis
 | volume = 2
 | year = 1988}}</ref> and <math>\theta_{\varepsilon_{\Omega_\omega + 1}}(0)</math> in Feferman's theta function, an ordinal collapsing function invented by Solomon Feferman.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Proof Theory |edition=2nd|first=Gaisi |last=Takeuti  |publisher=Dover Publications |isbn=978-0-486-32067-0 |year=2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Buchholz |first1=W. |title=⊨ISILC Proof Theory Symposion |contribution=Normalfunktionen und Konstruktive Systeme von Ordinalzahlen |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |date=1975 |volume=500 |pages=4–25 |doi=10.1007/BFb0079544 |contribution-url= |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-540-07533-2 |language=de}}</ref> It is the proof-theoretic ordinal of several formal theories:
* <math>\Pi_1^1\textsf{-CA} + \textsf{BI}</math>,<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Buchholz | first1 = Wilfried
 | last2 = Feferman | first2 = Solomon | author2-link = Solomon Feferman
 | last3 = Pohlers | first3 = Wolfram
 | last4 = Sieg | first4 = Wilfried
 | doi = 10.1007/bfb0091894
 | isbn = 3-540-11170-0
 | mr = 655036
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag, Berlin-New York
 | series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics
 | title = Iterated Inductive Definitions and Subsystems of Analysis: Recent Proof-Theoretical Studies
 | volume = 897
 | year = 1981}}</ref> a subsystem of [[second-order arithmetic]]
* <math>\Pi_1^1</math>-comprehension + transfinite induction<ref name=":1" />
* [[Buchholz's ID hierarchy|ID<sub>ω</sub>]], the system of ω-times iterated inductive definitions<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=ordinal analysis in nLab|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/ordinal+analysis#table_of_ordinal_analyses|access-date=2021-08-28|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>

== Definition ==
{{incomplete|the definition of the Takeuti-Feferman-Buchholz ordinal|date=April 2024}}

* Let <math>\Omega_\alpha</math> represent the smallest [[Uncountable set|uncountable]] ordinal with [[cardinality]] <math>\aleph_\alpha</math>.
* Let <math>\varepsilon_\beta</math> represent the <math>\beta</math>th [[Epsilon numbers (mathematics)|epsilon number]], equal to the <math>1+\beta</math>th fixed point of <math>\alpha \mapsto \omega^\alpha</math>
* Let <math>\psi</math> represent [[Buchholz psi functions|Buchholz's psi function]]
